(I approve of the PR)

As for the PR: I think the module doc-string should at least explain what a real closed field is, at the moment it says nothing really.

Yes, teaching reviewers how to click the Github "approve" button is super helpful. :-)

I'm still confused - my understanding was that the point of the bot assigning reviewers was so they could use maintainer-merge once review converged. Indeed that's been the workflow on previous PRs where I didn't want to bother anybody. If a non-reviewer is assigned, then there is no longer that delegated responsibility.
The assignment just indicates that this person will look at it. Everyone is welcome to do reviews, even if they aren't assigned as reviewers
I'm talking about the converse responsibility
Sorry I feel like I'm talking past everyone else, I'm genuinely just confused
I don't understand what you don't understand :)
i don't think assignment confers any formal responsibility? it's just a "this person should/will take a look"
Exact
I sometimes assign myself on PRs as a way to say "don't worry, someone is already reviewing this"

oh right I see
sorry I thought there was a level of (informal) responsibility assignment for the people with the power to do maintainer merges
the bot is just a system to make sure someone looks

#33942 - Support of a submonoid (part 1 of positive cone refactor) has been rewritten and is now up for review again
Is "support" a commonly used term in this setting?

There is, as far as I can tell, no consistent terminology. I took "support" from Lam's book on real algebra, and "pointed" and "generating" from the theory of convex cones (ie semimodules over the positive cone of an ordered ring).
However, I'm not an expert in real algebra or convex geometry, and I would be very happy to use terms preferred by experts.
I see: do you know of any other synonym? I'm just worried that this would conflict with the support of a function.
Not aware of any, sorry
#36863 - Support of a subsemiring (part 2 of positive cone refactor)
@Yakov Pechersky sorry for the ping, but you've been assigned to #34069 for a while now - are you able to leave a review? I split off some irrelevant stuff so the diff should be clean now.
I'm having some github issues atm. Do you need Algebra and algebraMap? Seems like this would be true for a monotone smul? Or if not, can you identify the additional axioms that make it necessary?

Yakov Pechersky said:

I'm having some github issues atm. Do you need Algebra and algebraMap? Seems like this would be true for a monotone smul? Or if not, can you identify the additional axioms that make it necessary?

I don't understand. I am proving that, under certain conditions, a linear order on an algebra yields an ordered module (defined as a monotone smul) iff the algebra map is monotone.

I saw your comment about preorder vs partial order. I'm asking about these variable hypotheses:

variable {α β : Type*} [CommSemiring α] [PartialOrder α] [Semiring β] [PartialOrder β] [Algebra α β]

Does it still work with just [SMul α β]?
You can't even state the theorems I added without Algebra, since they both contain algebraMap.

Something like

theorem IsOrderedModule.of_smul_one_mono [PosMulMono β] [MulPosMono β]
     (h : Monotone (fun x : alpha => (x \smul 1 : beta))) : IsOrderedModule α β where
Oh I see, dropping the commutativity assumption. Yeah that makes sense. I'll add the generalisations and ping you.
You were right - I was able to make a big generalisation. Thanks! Ready for review again.
Does the iff statement also have the same generalization or no?
I don't know. I only tried to generalise the new lemma I added. I can try to generalise the whole file?

Done! Opened a dependent PR:
#37040 - generalise ordered algebra lemmas
#37253 - correspondence between positive cones and group orderings
#37298 - unbundle group and ring cone
can someone explain the right way to remove the warnings? ^^
Does set_option backward.isDefEq.respectTransparency false in help?
These are warnings about deprecated declarations in deprecated theorems about those declarations. So, no it doesn't.

I guess I was looking at the

Note: The updated constant has a different type:
∀ (G : Type u_1) [inst : CommGroup G] [inst_1 : PartialOrder G] [inst_2 : IsOrderedMonoid G], (Submonoid.oneLE G).IsMulPointed
instead of
(H : Type u_2) → [inst : CommGroup H] → [inst_1 : PartialOrder H] → [IsOrderedMonoid H] → GroupCone H

These are warnings about deprecated declarations in deprecated theorems about those declarations. So, no it doesn't.

Is this preferred? Or should the declarations just be deleted instead (or something)?
I think this is preferred. I've written down that line untold amounts in my own deprecation PRs.

The maths in these PRs is an abstraction I made up to defne uniformly

  • positive cones in groups and rings
  • pointed cones in vector spaces over an ordered field
  • orderings in rings

The maths isn't hard, but it's unfamiliar, and in particular it's not obvious I defined things correctly (indeed I set things up wrong the first time I tried it, which is why these PRs even exist). I'm worried that this is why I'm struggling to get these two PRs reviewed. Fortunately after these it's back to standard maths.
I guess I can try and take another look
no don't worry! I'm more expressing a general concern I have with these PRs
